summary: A future at Depth (client a) and Quote (client b): an OI packet before the first full packet publishes nothing; after it, a circuit packet and an OI packet each republish the last full packet with only their own fields changed, never a zero price.

notes: Prices, the band 1350/1650 and OI 777 from the web tests; the book and OI 700 on the full packet are added, and each partial has its own packet time.

deviations.reason: The web sends the change since the previous close for every instrument (in LTP frames too); the desktop's common carrier sends it for indices only (audit C04, lane wire).

The HDFC Sky web adapter repeats ltp as last_price in every frame; the desktop's common carrier sends ltp only (a per-broker alias for lane wire).
The web sends the circuit band (from the full packet, refreshed by the *_CIRC packet) in Depth frames; the desktop decodes and merges it but its common carrier drops it (audit C06, P-11, lane wire).
Follows the broker's web adapter; set in the per-broker dialect entry (lane wire) in Phase B. The HDFC Sky web adapter puts no mode in its data; the desktop sends the label (ltp, quote, full).

The HDFC Sky web adapter repeats close as prev_close in every mode, LTP included; the desktop's common carrier sends close only, and in Quote and Depth only (a per-broker alias for lane wire). In an LTP frame built from an LTP-type packet the web's value is a proto3 0.0 (a web defect, see ltp_mode).

The web sends the packet's own time (packetTimestamp, or the index's packetTimeStamp) as timestamp; HdfcSkyFeed::events stamps the receipt time instead and uses the packet time only as the trade-time fallback (HDFC Securities' feed sends the packet time). A desktop defect.

The HDFC Sky web adapter sends the broker token as a string in every frame; the desktop's common carrier has no such field. Lead decision: carry it as a per-broker extra, or record it as a desktop decision.
